H0CO03165.name: Lauren Boebert
H0CO03165.bio: U.S. Representative running to represent Colorado's 4th District in Congress.

H6CO04202.name: Eileen Laubacher
H6CO04202.bio: Retired U.S. Navy rear admiral who served 34 years, including as Senior Director for South Asia on the National Security Council.

positions.stance: Supports ending tariffs that raise prices on fuel, fertilizer, equipment and groceries, enacting middle-class tax cuts, and cracking down on price gouging.
Supports expanding telehealth, letting Medicaid negotiate lower prices on more drugs, and capping insulin at $35 per month for everyone.
Would reverse Medicaid cuts that threaten rural hospitals, protect the 340B Drug Pricing Program, and recognize EMS as an essential service.
Supports passing a long-term Farm Bill and initiatives helping young people start or take over family farms.
Supports term limits and age limits, banning members of Congress from trading stocks, and ending dark money in campaigns.

H6CO05142.name: Jeff Crank
H6CO05142.bio: Member of Congress for Colorado's Fifth District who has worked in El Paso County for more than 30 years.

H6CO05324.name: Jessica Killin
H6CO05324.bio: U.S. Army veteran and lawyer who worked as a USAA executive and later served in roles on Capitol Hill and at the White House.

positions.stance: Would "end irrational tariffs that are raising prices" and work to stop price gouging by oil and grocery company CEOs and corporate landlords.
Supports banning stock trading by members of Congress, ending congressional pay during shutdowns, and overturning Citizens United.
Would increase staffing at VA clinics and restore full funding for the Veterans Crisis Line.
Would repeal Medicaid cuts, protect Medicare, allow Medicare to negotiate more drug prices, and cap insulin at $35 for everyone.
Supports balancing the budget, paying down the national debt, and making corporations and the very wealthy pay their fair share while cutting middle-class taxes.

H8CO06229.name: Jason Crow
H8CO06229.bio: Member of Congress and Army veteran who served three combat tours in Iraq and Afghanistan, rising from private to captain.

positions.stance: Supports investing in workforce development, apprenticeship training, and growing industries like healthcare, technology and renewable energy to bring high-paying jobs to the 6th District.
Promises not to take corporate PAC money and wants to end "the flood of unlimited and undisclosed money" in politics, citing his End Dark Money Act.
Supports policies to improve law enforcement, reduce incarceration, decriminalize marijuana, and adopt data-based reforms such as restorative justice.
Says democratic institutions and the rule of law must be defended; cosponsored the Voting Rights Advancement Act to protect eligible Americans' right to vote.
Opposes school funding cuts and voucher proposals, and supports affordable student loans, refinancing, and loan forgiveness for public service careers.

H6CO06165.name: Jason Clark
H6CO06165.bio: West Point graduate who has been an entrepreneur and small business owner in Aurora, Colorado, for more than 30 years.

positions.stance: Calls the cost of rent, education, and healthcare "unsustainable for too many Coloradans" and says addressing rising costs is his top priority.
Supports jobs across Colorado by embracing entrepreneurs, small businesses, and developers.
Would "go after the criminals" and "clean up Colfax Avenue."

H8CO07045.name: Brittany Pettersen
H8CO07045.bio: Former Colorado state senator who chaired the Colorado House Education Committee.

positions.stance: Would help small businesses recover by increasing access to capital and invest in research, technology, infrastructure and rural broadband.
Sponsored price-gouging legislation as a state senator and says she will do the same in Congress to reduce costs for working families.
Would fight to repeal the 2017 Trump tax cuts "that only benefited the wealthy and largest corporations" and give breaks to the middle class.
Wants national equal-pay and retirement-savings policies and federal investment to help families afford "the skyrocketing cost of childcare."
Supports loan forgiveness in fields like education and health care and funding apprenticeship programs and job training.

H6CO07122.name: Tim Bennett
H6CO07122.bio: Retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel and Ranger with nearly 30 years of military service and a sitting school board member.

positions.stance: Supports prioritizing mothers, defending parental authority, and making having a family "affordable and safe."
Supports making home ownership possible, reducing inflation, and bringing "well paying jobs and business back to Colorado."
Would "stop reckless federal spending" and "stop and reverse sending America's wealth overseas."
Will ask of every bill, "Will this make life more affordable for the people of CD-7?" and oppose it if the answer is no.
Would protect Colorado water rights and strengthen storage and infrastructure "without imposing one-size-fits-all solutions from Washington."

H4CO08034.name: Gabe Evans
H4CO08034.bio: Congressman for Colorado's 8th District, former Army Black Hawk pilot, former Arvada police officer, and former Colorado state representative.

positions.stance: Would "lower the cost of living by reining in deficit spending and the tax-and-regulate policies that are crushing our economy."
Would "ensure our military is focused on warfighting and not politically correct agendas."
Supports educational freedom so "families can choose the education that works best for them."
Would "protect freedom of expression, defend the Second Amendment, and secure the rights of all Americans."

H6CO08013.name: Manny Rutinel
H6CO08013.bio: Attorney, former Colorado state representative, and former economist for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

positions.stance: Would expand tax credits for working parents, make billionaires pay what they owe, close corporate tax loopholes, and lower drug, premium and energy costs.
Would oppose any attempt to cut Social Security or Medicare or raise the retirement age, and make the wealthy pay their fair share.
Would expand Medicare's power to negotiate drug prices and cap insulin at $35 a month for every American who needs it.
Says housing is "a basic life necessity" and that a full-time paycheck should cover food and rent.
Would expand VA cancer treatment coverage for exposure to radiation, burn pits or water contamination, and expand suicide prevention and peer support programs.

H2MN01223.name: Brad Finstad
H2MN01223.bio: Fourth-generation farmer and lifelong resident of southern Minnesota serving in Congress.

positions.stance: Wants federal farm policy that avoids burdensome obstacles and is "written by farmers, for farmers," opposing policies like California's Proposition 12.
Opposes reckless government spending and burdensome taxes; aims to keep more money in paychecks and give small businesses certainty.
Supports keeping the border secure, resuming construction of the southern border wall, and alleviating Customs and Border Patrol staffing shortages.
Supports safeguards so that only U.S. citizens can vote in federal elections, including proof-of-citizenship requirements to register.

H6MN01190.name: Jake Johnson
H6MN01190.bio: Math teacher from Stewartville in Southern Minnesota.

positions.stance: Would vote to end tariffs and the Iran War driving up grocery, gas and fertilizer prices, and cut red tape to build homes and expand childcare.
Supports tax cuts for working families and small businesses, paid for by raising taxes and closing loopholes for big corporations and the super wealthy.
Supports a balanced budget amendment and would vote against raising the debt ceiling until the budget is balanced.
Supports term limits, a ban on pardons for family and donors, and banning members of Congress from selling stocks and becoming lobbyists.
Supports passing a bipartisan farm bill, farmers' right to repair equipment, and undoing recent cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.

H6MN02230.name: Matt Little
H6MN02230.bio: Former Mayor of Lakeville, former Minnesota state senator, and owner of a law firm representing seniors and people with disabilities.

positions.stance: Supports a moratorium on data centers and regulating AI, saying Big Tech wants to "drain our aquifers, gobble up our farmland, and hand the bill to taxpayers."
Is "fighting to get ICE out of Minnesota now," saying ICE agents have shown "a callous indifference to the value of life."
Wants an economy where prices are affordable and opportunities accessible "for everyone, not just the richest Americans," including a tax on the ultrawealthy.
Supports Medicare for All to make quality healthcare affordable and accessible for all Minnesotans.
Will "champion an end to violence, genocide, and war" to build a peaceful, prosperous future for Israel and Palestine.

H6MN02263.name: Eric Pratt
H6MN02263.bio: Minnesota state senator since 2012 and former Prior Lake–Savage school board member with a career in banking and business at Target and U.S. Bank.

positions.stance: In Congress, would focus on "lowering costs, supporting small businesses, and restoring stability" to the economy for working families.
Supports law enforcement and first responders and says laws should be enforced "fairly, responsibly, and consistently, from our neighborhoods to the U.S. border."
Would "crack down on fraud, abuse, and the people who exploit the system at everyone else's expense."

H4MN03118.name: Kelly Morrison
H4MN03118.bio: Physician who practiced as an OBGYN in Minnesota for more than 20 years and now represents Minnesota's Third District in Congress.

positions.stance: Is fighting to make healthcare "more affordable and accessible for all Americans" and opposes the Trump Administration's cuts to health care.
Has introduced legislation to exempt small businesses from tariffs and get them tariff refunds, and wants to make running a small business easier.
Opposes efforts to gut the VA and has introduced bills to expand veterans' fertility care and guarantee housing for all homeless veterans.
Believes Congress should lower the costs of healthcare, housing, and child care while investing in innovation, infrastructure, and entrepreneurship.
Champions clean air, clean water, and protecting public lands, and opposes the rollback of pollution regulations.

H6MN03170.name: Tyler Bass
H6MN03170.bio: Contractor and small business owner and former licensed health insurance agent.

positions.stance: Supports banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks while in office.
Wants tax dollars "spent on Americans first" and a plan to stop fraud, waste, and abuse in programs like Medicaid.
Wants "American workers hired first" and opposes policies that put foreign labor programs ahead of Minnesota workers.

H0MN04049.name: Betty McCollum
H0MN04049.bio: Member of Congress since 2000 and Dean of the Minnesota Congressional Delegation; former social studies teacher, North St. Paul city councilmember, and Minnesota state representative.

H6MN04293.name: Paul Wikstrom
H6MN04293.bio: Electrical engineer who has worked for 35 years in engineering and management roles at Minnesota medtech and aerospace companies.

positions.stance: Supports mandatory audits for all major federal spending and requiring fraud-prevention measures as a condition of funding.
Would eliminate tax on tips, end tax on overtime, expand child tax credits, and eliminate the death tax to protect farms and small businesses.
Would increase price transparency, allow buying insurance across state lines, and stop drug companies from blocking access to generics and imported drugs.
Would invest in domestic manufacturing and energy independence and require Congressional approval for major regulations under a one-in/two-out rule.
Supports real border security to stop fentanyl, expanded COPS and Byrne JAG grants, and tougher federal penalties for those who attack police.

H8MN05239.name: Ilhan Omar
H8MN05239.bio: Member of Congress representing Minnesota's 5th Congressional District.

positions.stance: Supports national anti-bullying legislation, banning conversion therapy, and preventing discrimination against LGBTQIA+ youth and families in foster care.
Would "abolish ICE," end deportation and detention programs she calls inhumane, oppose expanding the border wall, and protect sanctuary cities.
Would preserve funding for the National Endowment for the Arts, the National Endowment for the Humanities, and the Institute for Museums and Library Services.
Supports raising the national minimum wage to $17 an hour and establishing national paid family leave and sick days for every worker.
Would codify Roe v. Wade into federal law, repeal the Hyde Amendment, and protect access to contraception and IVF.

H6MN05357.name: John Nagel
H6MN05357.bio: Retired Minnesota State Patrol field lieutenant with a 30-year career at the State Patrol.

positions.stance: Says government is "too big, too wasteful, and too intrusive"; would cut taxes, fight inflation, and eliminate fraud and waste.
Would work to keep violent criminals off the streets, fully protect schools, and ensure police receive the funding and support they deserve.
Would fight to keep the border "locked down" while supporting legal immigration, faster processing, and rewarding those who follow the rules.
Wants schools to return to their core purpose of educating children, with classrooms focused "on learning, not indoctrination."
Will defend the Second Amendment and free speech and work to "unleash American energy" and end reliance on foreign adversaries.

H4MN06087.name: Tom Emmer
H4MN06087.bio: U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 6th Congressional District and House Majority Whip.

positions.stance: Focused on fighting the affordability crisis, restoring energy independence, and making the Trump tax cuts permanent, including no tax on tips and overtime.
Supports "peace through strength" policies and giving troops the resources they need to protect the country at home and abroad.
Dedicated to reducing Washington's runaway spending and favors "regular order" appropriations over bloated omnibus bills.
Believes "only Americans should vote in American elections" and supports the SAVE Act requiring proof of citizenship to register.
Backs the H.R. 2 border security bill to stop fentanyl, gangs, and terrorist threats, and the Laken Riley Act on deporting illegal aliens who commit crimes.

H6MN06215.name: Doug Chapin
H6MN06215.bio: Election policy expert and attorney who led The Pew Charitable Trusts' elections team and worked at the University of Minnesota's Humphrey School.

positions.stance: Will fight for single-payer healthcare "like Medicare for All" so people can get care without fear of going broke.
Supports withholding or restricting aid to Israel until it ends what he calls its war in Gaza.
Would eliminate the cap on Social Security taxes so wealthy taxpayers fully contribute.
Would fight to impeach HHS Secretary RFK Jr. and revive America's leadership in medical research and innovation.
Would vote to repeal tax cuts for billionaires so "everyone pays their fair share" and working families keep more of their money.

H0MN07091.name: Michelle Fischbach
H0MN07091.bio: Member of Congress and co-chair of the House Pro-Life Caucus; former Minnesota state senator.

positions.stance: Supports protecting "innocent human life at all stages from conception to natural death" and stopping federal funding for abortion.
Says the right to keep and bear arms "shall not be infringed. Period." and opposes confiscating guns from law-abiding citizens.
Supports law enforcement enforcing immigration laws and opposes efforts to abolish ICE and promote sanctuary cities.
Says government should never compel people to violate their religious beliefs or take away parental decision-making in healthcare, education or athletics.
Supports securing good trade deals for farmers, rebuilding rural infrastructure, protecting key tax policies, and investing in workforce development.

H6MN07312.name: Erik Osberg
H6MN07312.bio: Former small business owner and current county employee who has worked across the financial sector, public sector, media, and trades.

positions.stance: Will defend constitutional freedoms, protect fair elections, and make sure those in power "answer to the people."
Pledges to end the influence of Citizens United and refuses corporate PAC money.
Wants more affordable, accessible care by protecting rural hospitals and clinics and lowering prescription drug costs.
Believes every child should have access to a quality education "no matter their ZIP code" and supports students, teachers, and public schools.
Will fight for policies that support family farms, reduce unnecessary burdens, and protect rural economies.

H8MN08043.name: Pete Stauber
H8MN08043.bio: Member of Congress, former professional hockey player, and retired Duluth police officer of more than two decades.

positions.stance: Helped champion tax relief now in law and is working to reduce reckless spending and lower the cost of living for all Minnesotans.
Supports Border Patrol agents, strengthening law enforcement, and increasing construction and security measures along the border.
Focused on making America "energy and critical mineral dominant" to reduce dependence on foreign adversaries and strengthen national security.
"Will always stand for the unborn" and strongly opposes any efforts to use taxpayer funds for abortion.
Committed to protecting the Second Amendment right to defend your family and your home.

H6MN08179.name: Trina Swanson
H6MN08179.bio: Former federal official who spent two decades at the Department of Homeland Security with U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

positions.stance: "I will fight for universal healthcare"; would protect health insurance tax credits and cap prices of life-saving medications.
Supports mining and miners and would back copper-nickel mining "when impartial scientists and engineers say it can be done safely."
Wants antitrust laws enforced so a handful of companies can't drive up the cost of food, fuel, and everyday essentials.
"I will protect the Boundary Waters"; says decisions must follow hydrology, geology, and long-term impact.
Supports securing the border, hiring more immigration judges and officers, and permanent legal status for Dreamers with an earned path to citizenship.

H6SC01334.name: Jenny Costa Honeycutt
H6SC01334.bio: Attorney and small business owner on James Island who is a local elected Republican official.

positions.stance: Says every vote she takes "will be grounded in what's best for the Lowcountry – its families, its economy, and its way of life."
Will stand with law enforcement and secure the border to stop the flow of fentanyl and "criminal illegal aliens."
Would combat wasteful spending, end waste, fraud, and abuse of government programs, and work to balance the budget.
Will defend free speech, religious liberty, the separation of powers, and the Second Amendment, saying "the Bill of Rights is not negotiable."
Will be "a steadfast advocate for the unborn" and is committed to "keeping men out of women's sports."

H6SC01359.name: Nancy Lacore
H6SC01359.bio: Retired Navy vice admiral who served 35 years, beginning as a helicopter pilot and ending as Chief of Navy Reserve.

positions.stance: Would end tariffs on building materials, ban corporate landlords' algorithmic rent-pricing software, and support tax credits for first-time homebuyers' down payments.
Supports targeted tax credits for small businesses that hire or raise wages, simpler access to federal loans, and workforce training and apprenticeships.
Would restore enhanced ACA premium subsidies, reverse Medicaid cuts, expand Medicare drug price negotiation, and offer a non-profit insurance option like Medicare.
Would eliminate Trump's tariffs, support targeted trade enforcement instead of blanket tariffs, and require any tariffs to expire automatically.
Would cap childcare costs at 7% of a family's income with quarterly tax credits and expand tax credits for providers and employers.

H2SC02059.name: Joe Wilson
H2SC02059.bio: Congressman, former real estate attorney, 17-year South Carolina state senator, and retired Army Reserve and National Guard colonel.

positions.stance: Supports policies that "rein in Washington's waste, protect taxpayers," and put the country on a path to a genuinely balanced budget.
Believes in "peace through strength," championing investments in defense capability and support for allies to deter adversaries.
Supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy, including small modular reactors, next-generation nuclear technology, and responsible domestic production.
Pushes for faster benefits, expanded healthcare access, improved transition services, and accountability within the VA.
Stands for parent-driven education and sponsors Right to Work legislation preventing employees from being forced to pay union dues.

H6SC02159.name: Zyon Khalifa
H6SC02159.bio: Air Force reservist and former University of South Carolina track athlete from Aiken County who has worked as a mechanic.

positions.stance: Would attract sustainable industries and create incentives for businesses to invest in rural and underserved communities.
Supports grants and low-interest loans for small businesses and mentorship programs for aspiring entrepreneurs.
Supports a minimum wage increase "so that full-time workers can achieve financial stability and support their families."
Supports job training partnerships with local businesses and schools, and pathways that guide youth away from the prison pipeline toward careers.
Advocates increasing teacher pay, addressing the teacher shortage, and increasing funding for public schools.
